parts.title: Reading - Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage_text:
Last March I lost my camera while I was on a school trip to Portsmouth. I left it on the bus on our way back to our school. I called the bus company the day after to check if they could find it, but of course it wasn't there. My parents got really angry and told me they couldn't buy me a new one.

I knew my parents were right, so I decided I would get a new one by myself. I started thinking of ways to earn and save money. My parents give me £8 every week so the first thing I did was to keep my pocket money in a drawer in my bedroom.

I also offered to help my uncle Alan. He's often away for work, but he can't take his dog with him. I started to look after his dog when he wasn't at home. After some time, my uncle's neighbours saw me. They asked me if I could help with their cats, dogs and rabbits, too. So, I started working for three families living across the street.

In less than three months I had enough money to buy a camera. It was the same as the one I had lost but to me it was much better. I paid for it with what I earned and it felt very different. This experience taught me what it means to work hard and I learnt that you must be careful with the things you have because they take a lot of hard work.

questions.question: Where did Sandy lose her camera?
What did Sandy do?

options.A: She asked her parents for another camera.
options.B: She thought of ways to get money for a new camera.
options.C: She decided not to buy a new camera.

questions.question: What was the first job she got?

options.B: Keeping her uncle's dog at her house.
options.C: Taking care of her uncle's pet.

questions.question: What else did she do to make more money?

options.A: She started working for other families with pets.
options.B: She looked after her uncle's cats and rabbits.
options.C: She helped her neighbours with housework.

questions.question: The camera she bought was

options.A: more expensive than the last one.
options.B: as good as the last one.

parts.title: Listening - Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one word or a number or a date or a time.
parts.context: You will hear a teacher telling some boys and girls about a photo competition.
parts.transcript:
Hello, everyone. I'm going to tell you about this year's photo competition: as you know, last year's photos were about travel; this year, however, students have to take pictures about nature. You can choose to take a photo of animals or plants and send it to the school office from July 23rd to the 28th. The competition will be on the last Tuesday of July.
The students who want to take part in the competition must send two photos, but only one will be chosen. The winners will receive an email message before the competition day. There will be three prizes: the third prize is a cap; the second prize is a T-shirt and the winner of this year's competition will get a backpack.
Remember to tell your family and friends that the photo exhibition will be on the fourth floor of the school. Now, if you have any questions, I'll be happy to answer all of them.

parts.title: Listening - Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear Monica and her friend Jonathan talking about a holiday.

questions.question: Where did Jonathan spend his holiday?
When did they leave?
What does Quentin say about Yellowstone Park?

options.B: It's America's most exciting national park.

questions.question: What was he afraid of at the campsite?
What is Quentin unhappy about?

options.A: He spent too much on souvenirs.

parts.transcript:
Monica: Hi Jonathan. So, the holidays are over, back to school again…
Jonathan: I know, but I had a great one this year.
Monica: Where did you go?
Jonathan: Well, my mother loves Canada and Dad really wanted to visit Brazil, but we finally booked flights to the USA.
Monica: Lucky you! How long did you stay there?
Jonathan: We went in the first week of the holiday, on the 3rd of July and came back on the 30th. We toured several places like Niagara Falls and New York, but the best was Yellowstone Park.
Monica: Wow, what's that like?
Jonathan: Well, it was really exciting. It's the oldest national park in the USA and it's really big. At times it was a bit scary too. We spent some nights at a campsite in the park. We were worried the bears might come at night! Anyway, we saw lots of wild birds, foxes and a lot of other wild animals. We even saw a snake in a river, but it wasn't a dangerous one.
Monica: Did your brother enjoy the holiday?
Jonathan: Yes, he did but he spent too much money on souvenirs. I only got a few. However, I didn't take enough photos. That was a mistake!

Boy: Actually, I stopped a few weeks ago. I didn't really like it so I changed to something I enjoy more.
Girl: I guess it's about chess.

Girl: Well, I think I'd prefer to learn a new sport, but of course we're all different.

parts.title: Listening - Part 5
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.context: You will hear Sam talking to his father about school subjects. Which subject does each of his classmates like?

questions.key_pdf_note: KEY.pdf prints 25 A, though transcript says 'He's really into Science and wants to be a scientist' (H). Both H and A are noted.

parts.transcript:
Father: How was school today, Sam?
Sam: Our German teacher got really angry this morning!
Father: Why?
Sam: Well, nobody except Toby likes this subject. Every time the German teacher talks, all my classmates start chatting.
Father: Really? Even you?
Sam: Well, you know I'm not very keen on German… I prefer English.
Father: What about Jessica? She spent some months in Germany, right?
Sam: Yes, she did, so now she says it's too easy for her and she gets bored. She has started Italian and she loves it.
Father: Well, she's obviously good at languages.
Sam: Yes, not like Marina, who is hopeless at English! She prefers doing Maths exercises!
Father: Your Maths teacher will be pleased about that!
Sam: Her brother is different, he loves Art. He's brilliant at drawing.
Father: Who's this clever boy?
Sam: Oh, Dad, it's Henry! Don't you remember? He came here with his friend, Colin, a week ago. He's in my class, too.
Father: Oh yes, he's a good football player. He must like PE best.
Sam: No. He's really into Science and wants to be a scientist.
